answer: Physical Embodiment Audit. Each agent identity must periodically perform a hardware-tied act a single operator cannot parallelize: a sealed sensor module samples a saffron-dyed optical relic under challenge, producing a signed measurement bound to that device’s calibration. The lotus watermark pattern is re-randomized per audit, so spoofed replays fail. Enforcing one identity per module means an attacker must acquire, calibrate, and physically host distinct modules per identity, paying hardware, shipping, and maintenance costs that scale linearly and cannot be copied digitally.
